supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Anthropic to rent AI computing power from Nscale for $45 billion, source says
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports, citing a person familiar with the matter, that Anthropic will spend about $45 billion over six years for roughly 460 MW of Nscale capacity in West Virginia using NVIDIA Vera Rubin systems. Anthropic declined to comment.

supportingEvidence.title: Financial Times: Anthropic agrees $45bn AI data centre deal with Nscale
supportingEvidence.note: FT independently reports a six-year, roughly $45 billion agreement tied to about 460 MW at Nscale's West Virginia campus.

supportingEvidence.title: Nscale primary source: Monarch West Virginia campus and Vera Rubin deployment plan
supportingEvidence.note: Nscale confirms the Monarch campus, its planned 1.35 GW Phase 1 scale and Vera Rubin deployment architecture, independently validating that the physical site and technology stack described in the reports are real.

supportingEvidence.title: Anthropic primary source: $50 billion U.S. AI infrastructure investment program
supportingEvidence.note: Anthropic previously announced a separate $50 billion U.S. data-center investment program, supporting the broader thesis that it is aggressively securing domestic compute, but this is not confirmation of the Nscale contract.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: Anthropic declined to comment on the reported deal
contradictingEvidence.note: No Anthropic or Nscale primary announcement found in this cycle confirms the reported $45 billion commitment, its exact commercial structure, milestone protections or final enforceability.

contradictingEvidence.title: Nscale primary source: Monarch already has a separate Microsoft framework
contradictingEvidence.note: Nscale's published Monarch plans include a separate Microsoft LOI and staged buildout beginning in late 2027, so reported future capacity should not be assumed to be immediately delivered or fully utilized.

falsifier: Downgrade or remove the reported-commitment thesis if Anthropic or Nscale denies the deal, later primary disclosures materially change the value/capacity/term, or the Monarch capacity is delayed/cancelled. Downgrade the productive-demand interpretation if deployed capacity materially exceeds utilization or Anthropic's realized product economics fail to justify the commitment.
title: Reported $45B Anthropic-Nscale lease pushes frontier AI toward utility-scale compute commitments
summary: Reuters and FT report that Anthropic is committing roughly $45 billion over six years for about 460 MW of Nscale compute in West Virginia using NVIDIA Vera Rubin systems. The physical Nscale campus is primary-confirmed, but the Anthropic contract itself remains unconfirmed by either company, so Nexus should treat this as REPORTED_COMMITMENT rather than CONFIRMED_CONTRACT.
delta: Upgrade multi-year frontier-model compute demand and capital intensity, while preserving the source-state distinction: reported commercial commitment is not the same as primary-confirmed contract. For AI-demand-quality analysis, separate contracted capacity, financed capacity, deployed capacity, utilized capacity and productive capacity.
firstOrderImpacts: stronger forward demand signal for Vera Rubin systems, networking, power and data-center construction if the commitment is confirmed
greater concentration of frontier-model economics in long-duration infrastructure commitments
higher sensitivity of model-company economics to power, utilization, financing terms and infrastructure delivery risk
secondOrderImpacts: AI infrastructure increasingly resembles utility-scale project finance rather than ordinary software hosting
Nexus should track compute commitments as staged state transitions instead of treating announced spend as productive capacity
power-site provenance and project delivery may become as important as model benchmark performance for forecasting frontier-AI economics

alphaHunter.hypothesis: Tracking the transition from reported/contracted AI compute commitments to delivered and utilized capacity predicts infrastructure winners and demand durability better than headline capex announcements alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: reported AI capex and compute-contract headline value
alphaHunter.alternativeData: site energization milestones, GPU delivery timing, power capacity, utilization proxies, model/API revenue growth, financing structure and project delays
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 6-18 month forecast accuracy for delivered compute, utilization, revenue productivity and supplier demand versus headline-capex baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the added infrastructure-state layer if it fails to improve held-out forecasts of delivered/utilized capacity or if the data arrives too late to change decisions.
